title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC0RB_1LD0LD_1RA1LE_---0LF_1LB1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC0RB_1LD0LD_1RA1LE_---0LF_1LB1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is understood at the level of words: at the left turn the tape is blocks of ones separated by single 0s; between round trips the whole tape except a chaotic zone of about 450 to 610 cells at the right end slides 16 cells left unchanged, and the left end gains one copy of the word 1^5 0 1^6 0 1^4 0 1 0 per round trip. The sweep rules are proved in Lean; the right-end engine is not understood, and the machine can halt only inside it or at a turn.
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (10,000 by the kernel alone); the C simulator finds none in 10<sup>9</sup>.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 74,489 cells have been visited and 56,218 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: Five-to-thirteen-step shift rules of the two sweeps, for every repeat count and any tape around: B erases a block of ones going right (b_erase), F keeps one going left (f_ones), and B crosses the words 1101111 and 101111 of the right sweep.

claims.title: Left end: one more copy of a word per round trip
claims.text: At every left turn after about 2·105 steps the tape starts 0 1^4 0 1^4 0 1^3 0 1^8 0 1^6 0 1^4 0 1 0 1^5 0 1^9 0 1^4 0 1 0 (1^5 0 1^6 0 1^4 0 1 0)^n and n grows by one per round trip (n = 61 at 2.96·106 steps).

claims.title: A translating archive
claims.text: Compared with the previous left turn, all of the tape but its first 67 cells and a zone at the right end is the same word moved 16 cells to the left (3,324 of 3,833 cells at 2.96·10<sup>6</sup> steps).

claims.title: The engine stays small
claims.text: The changing zone at the right end (compared with the previous left turn moved 16 cells) is 450 cells wide at 1.9·10<sup>7</sup> steps, 577 at 2.1·10<sup>8</sup>, 609 at 2.0·10<sup>9</sup>, 605 at 3.0·10<sup>9</sup>, while the tape grows to 128,771 cells.

claims.title: The halt needs 0 D>1
claims.text: The only halting transition E0 is reached from D reading 1 with a 0 on its left. In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps D reads a 1 49,299,233 times, each time with a 1 on its left.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would have to control the right-end engine: show that the cells it leaves behind never change again and that it never writes 0 1 where D arrives. Its width looks bounded but creeps up slowly; no invariant for it is known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 74,489 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).
After 109 steps the tape spans 74,489 cells (33,633 left of the start, 20,857 right), with a density of 1s of 0.755.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A frozen trail and a small engine
html: Look at the tape each time the head turns at the left end, and draw the rows one under the other, each row slid 16 cells to the right of the one before. Almost everything then stands still: vertical stripes. Only a narrow band at the right edge flickers.

So the machine is a translating archive: between two round trips the tape is the same word moved 16 cells to the left, except for the first 67 cells (where one more copy of 1^5 0 1^6 0 1^4 0 1 0 appears per round trip) and a zone at the right end of 450 to 610 cells that keeps changing. That zone is the engine: it moves to the right with the edge of the tape and the cells it leaves behind never change again.

sections.heading: Two ways to write the same blocks
html: At a left turn the tape is blocks of ones separated by single 0s, for example 0 1^4 0 1^4 0 1^3 0 1^8 …. The rightward sweep turns each block into runs of exactly three ones separated by runs of 0s (at the right turn the tape looks like 1^6 0^2 1^3 0 1^3 0^2 1^3 0^3 …); the leftward sweep turns them back. Each sweep is a sequence of shift rules, proved in Lean for every repeat count:

rulefromtowhat it does
b_eraseL B> (1)^n RL (0)^n B> RRightward sweep: B erases a block of ones.
f_onesL (1)^n F> 1 RL F> 1 (1)^n RLeftward: F runs left over a block of ones, keeping them.
b_wordL B> (1101111)^n RL (1110000)^n B> RRightward: B crosses the word 1101111 (a block 1^4 after 1^2) and leaves 1110000.
b_word2L 0 B> (101111)^n RL (111000)^n 0 B> RRightward: B, with a 0 behind it, crosses 101111 and leaves 111000.

sections.heading: Only the engine can stop it
html: The machine halts only from D reading a 1 with a 0 on its left (0 D>1). In the first 109 steps D reads a 1 about 49 million times, always with a 1 on its left. The frozen part of the tape is crossed by the sweep rules and cannot produce the pattern; the engine at the right end could. The engine is small (about 600 cells) but chaotic, and it never repeats, since the trail it leaves is not periodic. Deciding this machine means understanding that engine.

summary: A translating archive: everything but a ~500-cell engine at the right end slides 16 cells left per round trip, while the left end grows a periodic word (5 6 4 1)^n.
family: translating archive with a chaotic right-end engine

sections.heading: How it works
paragraphs: At the moment the head turns at the left end, the tape is a row of blocks of ones separated by single 0s. The rightward sweep rewrites each block into runs of three ones separated by runs of 0s; the leftward sweep rebuilds blocks, with short zigzags. Both sweeps are lists of shift rules proved in lean/Rules.lean.

Over a round trip almost nothing changes: the tape between the first 67 cells and the last 450–610 is the same word as before, slid 16 cells to the left, and the left end gains one copy of 1^5 0 1^6 0 1^4 0 1 0. All the activity is in a small chaotic engine at the right end, which moves right with the tape's edge and leaves a frozen, non-periodic trail. Whether that engine can ever write the one pattern that halts (D reading a 1 with a 0 on its left) is the open question.
